subject: Sustained elongation on /generate endpoints — urgent triage

From: Alex Peterson <alex.peterson@clearspring.com>

Cc: platform@clearspring.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Degraded p99 on /generate — observed spike since 11/4

Hi Lauren,

We started seeing a sustained spike in p99 latency on our /generate and /batch/generate endpoints starting late 11/4. Impact: interactive agents at ClearSpring see slow responses for a subset of requests (p50 fine, p95 elevated ~800ms, p99 up to 9s). We also observed an increase in 503s at the same timeframe.

Attached a small sample of traces (p99-traces.csv) and a slide summarizing customer-visible impact. Key observations from our side:
- Tail latency correlates with request bursts hitting the concurrency cap for our tenant.
- Error rate spikes (503) appear when queue depth grows beyond configured window.
- Throughput overall hasn't dropped but a minority of requests are delayed significantly.

This is business-impacting for our checkout assistant. We need a clear mitigation plan and timeline. Can you loop in SRE/engineering and confirm next steps?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Peterson
Engineering Manager, ClearSpring Retail

Subject: Re: Degraded p99 on /generate — initial triage + temporary mitigations

Thanks for the ping, Lauren. Quick triage summary based on the traces and our telemetry:
- Root cause (probable): per-tenant concurrency cap combined with a bursty distribution of long-sequence requests is causing request queuing at the gateway. When queue depth exceeds the dequeue window we see 503s and extreme tail latencies.
- Contributing factors: intermittent KV-cache thrash for certain prompt prefixes (causes additional GPU work), and one model variant in your catalog that has ~2x token-processing variance at longer sequences.

Recommended immediate actions (can be executed within 30-90 minutes):
1) Temporary concurrency uplift for ClearSpring tenant from 50 -> 120 for the next 24h (requires ops approval). This should reduce queueing and bring p99 down.
2) Enable prefix-level KV caching for the most common prompt patterns (safe, reversible).
3) Route highest-latency traffic to a compatible but lower-variance model variant while we analyze the quantization/kernel path.
4) Short-term retention of full request traces for 72h (for post-mortem).

Attached: p99-traces.csv (sample), and a draft mutual_action_plan.docx that Marissa/Aditya can use in comms.

I'll start the uplift runbook and ETA — ops lead estimates ~45 minutes to complete change if approvals are fast. If we need more sustained capacity, I'll propose moving this workload to a small dedicated pool for ClearSpring (ops + account team approval required).

Hannah Schmitt
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
